summary: The article argues that Kevin Durant, despite elite talent and a résumé with two titles, two Finals MVPs and four scoring titles, is one of the most disrespected and polarizing superstars in NBA history. It attributes the criticism to his thin skin, his 2017 burner-account incident, his frequent team changes, his lack of titles since leaving the Warriors, and above all his 2016 decision to join the team that beat him.
one_line: An opinion piece examining why Kevin Durant, one of the NBA's most talented scorers, draws so much criticism, from his Warriors move to his title drought.
key_facts: Kevin Durant was drafted by the Seattle SuperSonics in 2007 with the No.2 pick.
Durant is a 6'11" forward known for his jump-shot and three-point accuracy, described as a true "Unicorn."
Durant has 27,393 regular-season points, ranking 11th in NBA history, and 4,878 playoff points, ranking 7th all-time.
Durant's résumé includes two NBA titles, two NBA Finals MVP awards, four scoring titles, and multiple All-Star and All-NBA selections.
Charles Barkley called Durant "sensitive" in a 60 Minutes interview, saying he is part of a generation that "thinks he can't be criticized."
In 2017 Durant used a burner account on Twitter to defend himself and was exposed when he accidentally posted a tweet from his verified account.
Durant has not won an NBA title since leaving the Warriors in 2019.
The Brooklyn trio of Durant, Kyrie Irving and James Harden lost in the second round of the 2021 playoffs to the Milwaukee Bucks.
The Nets traded Durant to the Suns at the trade deadline after he requested a trade; he fell short of a title in Phoenix despite teammates Devin Booker and Chris Paul.
In the 2016 Western Conference finals, Durant's OKC Thunder led the 73-9 Warriors 3-1 but lost the series in seven games.
In the 2016 offseason Durant joined the Warriors, leading many to label him a "snake" and "spineless."
Critics say Durant rode Stephen Curry's coattails to his two championships.
